name: Heun++2
plain: Looks two schedule entries ahead, evaluates the model at both, and blends three slopes with weights set by how far σ has fallen from the very first sigma. Weight shifts toward the first slope as σ drops, so late steps move toward Euler. Costs three model calls for most steps but moves x only one step each time.
math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
x₂=x+d·dt, dt=σ'−σ̂; D₂ at σ'. x₃=x₂+d₂(σ''−σ'), D₃ at σ''=sigmas[i+2].
w₂=σ'/(3σ₀), w₃=σ''/(3σ₀), w₁=1−w₂−w₃, σ₀=sigmas[0]. x'=x+dt(w₁d+w₂d₂+w₃d₃).
Near end (σ''=s_end): two-slope w₂=σ'/(2σ₀), w₁=1−w₂. Last step (σ'=s_end): Euler.
Optional churn before the model call (defaults off; no core node exposes s_churn): γ=min(s_churn/N, √2−1) when s_tmin≤σ≤s_tmax, N=len(sigmas)−1; σ̂=σ(1+γ); x←x+ε·s_noise·√(σ̂²−σ²), ε from torch.randn_like (global RNG, not the seeded noise sampler). All later σ in the step are σ̂.

props.stages: 3; 2 on penultimate; 1 on last (total 3N−3 for N≥2)
props.final_sigma0: Test is against s_end=sigmas[-1], not zero. With σ'=0 the Euler step equals D. With a nonzero end the last step is still Euler.
props.flow_const: No branch; weights use raw σ.

label: from code
surprise: Weights divide by sigmas[0], so a split or partial-denoise schedule changes the blend for the same σ; ε is drawn every step even with churn off, consuming global RNG.
